text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

SBC Warburg, which grabbed just over a third of the A$32.4 billion in deals undertaken last year, has risen to the top of Australia's league of takeover advisers, compiled by Corporate Adviser Securities Data, and is expected to be a major beneficiary of the expected increase in mergers and acquisitions this year. Page 1.

Mining industry analysts said last night the increase in production in all RTZ-CRA's major products, except borates, would be tempered by the stronger Australian dollar and softer commodity prices in 1996, and they predicted a static profit result for the end of the year, but the mining giant says it still expects to match its 1995 profits. Page 16.

In a controversial critique of a report presented to the Federal Government by a Government-appointed committee which has been reviewing the Standard Telephone Service, leading economist Professor Henry Ergas says providing access to digital data services for all Australians by 2000 could impose capital costs on the telecommunications industry of up to A$2.5 billion and lead to higher charges for residential consumers. Page 1.

Newcrest Mining managing director John Quinn said the board was yet to consider how the ill-fated A$470 million foray into rival Normandy would be recorded, but he admitted Newcrest faces huge losses from the investment. The group also posted an operating loss in the December quarter following problems at its flagship Telfer mine. Page 15.

Following news that BHP representatives indicated during investor presentations in Europe last week the company would sell A$4 billion in assets in the next 24 months, speculation has increased that BHP has decided to quit its 37 per cent stake in Foster's Brewing Group Ltd. Page 15.

Rothschild Australia was last night scrambling to correct an error contained in a letter Rothschild sent to shareholders which significantly understated the portfolio performance of major competitor Australian Foundation Investment Company. Rothschild said AFIC had returned 4.2 per cent to shareholders in the financial year to 1995-96, instead of the real figure of 15.9 per cent. Page 17.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following the release of Australia's lowest inflation result in two years, the dollar fell more than half a cent yesterday and speculation increased that the Reserve Bank would tighten monetary policy soon after its next meeting on February 4. Page 21.

Newcrest Mining managing director John Quinn said the company's Cadia project in New South Wales was shaping up as a "very major discovery" following the release of stunning drilling results yesterday. Quinn said the latest results from the Ridgeway depost could add significant new reserves. Page 21.

Seven Network chairmen Kerry Stokes said yesterday Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer was performing according to its business plan and he denied reports Seven might sell its investment in the MGM movie studio, as well as speculation that production plans would require extra shareholder funding. Page 21.

In an interview with The Australian yesterday, Crown CROA.X executive chairman Lloyd Williams, the main shareholder and joint-managing director of Hudson Conway Ltd, intensified speculation about the possibility of an eventual merger between Crown and Sydney Harbour Casino by ruling out any involvement by HudCon in SHC. Page 21.

As the newly merged St George-Advance Bank opened for business yesterday it received an upgraded credit rating from New York-based ratings agency Standard & Poor's, which had previously placed St George on credit-watch after the A$2.65 billion merger with Advance was announced in October last year. Page 23.

Southcorp Packaging executive general manager Barry Watts revealed yesterday Southcorp Holdings looks set to add value to its A$162 million purchase of Smorgon Consolidated Industries' PET plastics business by acquiring a 50 per cent share of its recycling technology company Inpet, a move Watts says will enable Southcorp to explore advanced PET recycling and production technology. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Speculation that the Reserve Bank will cut interest rates was intensified yesterday after the release of low inflation data that saw the Australia dollar plunge to a ten-month low, and share prices rise. However, amid concerns the market will be unable t absorb an extra A$3 billion in Federal Government bond issues to cover the blow-out in the Budget deficit, bond yields were little changed. Page 29.

A sluggish Advance Bank net profit for the six months to November 1996 has taken some of the glory out the final consummation of St George Bank's takeover of the company. It has also been confirmed Advance shareholders will not receive the full $2.65 bilion originally flagged as St George's offer. Page 29.

ACT Chief Minister Kate Carnell yesterday urged the Sydney investment community not to ignore Canberra, declaring the ACT's economy is 'in the middle of the tunnel' and the outlook is improving, despite the onset of recession and a glut of property. Page 31.

Optus Communications is set to hold a crucial board meeting in Melbourne today. Among the topics on today's agenda are the long-term future of pay-TV and local telephony group Optus Vision, funding of the Australian Rugby League and the Channel 7 litigation. Page 31.

A recent survey by the Australian Institute of Company Directors, conducted last November and released yesterday, has revealed superannuation is the key to increasing the nation's savings, but is also in dire need of simplification, with the administrativ burden of the new 15 per cent tax on super fund contributors by high-income earners a highly criticised aspect of the system. Page 31.

The share price of diversified group Southcorp yesterday rose six cents to close at a record A$4.31 after the group announced it had acquired 50 per cent of Innovations in PET (Inpet) from Smorgon Consolidated Industries - the other 50 per cent is owned b SWIG Pty Ltd. Page 33
THE AGE

German chemicals giant Hoechst announced yesterday it plans to sell its Altona plastics business to Kemcor Australia as part of the group's long-term global restructuring, and Hoechst Australia managing director Jens Mohr says Australia's low-tariff polic is a key reason why the group decided to quit its local plastics industry. Page B1.

A ban on high-rollers at the Reef Casino in Cairns has been extended until a restructure to save the Reef Casino Trust RCT.AX from receivership is finalised - the requirements for which include an injection of at least A$40 million to reduce the trust's debt from A$105 million. Page B1.

Narelle Hopper, an apprentice diesel fitter mechanic and one of the first women to work down the mines in Mount Isa, has won almost A$50,000 for sexual harassment after taking her complaints of constant sexual harassment when she was first employed at Mout Isa in 1992 to the Queensland Anti-Discrimination Tribunal. Page B1.

Appearing in the Human Rights and Equal Opportunity Commission in Sydney yesterday, Castrol's legal counsel, Chris Ronalds, denied that the oil giant allowed the sexual harassment of two female laboratory technicians at its Guildford plant in western Sydney. Page B1.

Following the announcement that it had acquired 50 per cent of Innovations in PET (Inpet), which holds the world's rights to the revolutionary Renew recycling process, from Smorgon Consolidated Industries for an undisclosed sum, shares in diversified packging group Southcorp rose six cents yesterday to close at a record A$4.31. Page B1.

Despite recording a rise in net income from US$511,000 to US$8.76 million in this fourth quarter, and a doubling in revenue from US$41.6 million to US$115.1 million, Netscape Communications Corp executives warned yesterday that the company's revenue growth would slow. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
